mstts:express-as.prosody: Imagine for a moment that beneath all the routines and choices of daily life, there’s a hidden world—a place where unexpected connections and subtle incentives quietly shape everything we do. What if tiny decisions and overlooked motivations were actually the secret forces guiding our neighborhoods, our jobs, even the way we raise our kids? That’s the fascinating perspective we get to explore together in Freakonomics: A Rogue Economist Explores the Hidden Side of Everything, written by Steven D. Levitt. Instead of just accepting things at face value, we’re invited to dig deeper, to look at how things like crime rates, real estate deals, or even sumo wrestling might actually be connected by the logic of incentives—sometimes in ways that totally surprise us. We’ll follow the data, challenge some old assumptions, and watch as what seemed random suddenly makes perfect sense. Through real stories and clever questions, we’re going to discover a whole new way of understanding why people and institutions act the way they do. Get ready to see familiar things in a completely fresh light, and maybe even start asking your own questions about how the world really works. Let’s dive in and uncover the hidden side of everything—together.
